title: Microsoft Offers Voluntary Buyouts to 60,000 Employees Across Four Countries
excerpt: The Voluntary Exit Offer covers about a quarter of Microsoft's 223,000-person workforce in the U.S., Canada, India and the U.K., with decisions due in the first week of December.
body:
• Microsoft is offering a Voluntary Exit Offer to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its 223,000-person workforce, according to GeekWire and Reuters.
  • The offer covers eligible staff at level 70 and below in the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom, on participating teams only.
  • Eligible employees have until the first week of December to decide; the package equals Microsoft's standard severance, including base pay by tenure and level, continued stock vesting and healthcare for a fixed period.
  • The program follows a spring voluntary retirement offer taken by about 30% of 8,750 eligible U.S. employees, and July layoffs of 4,800 jobs.

Microsoft is offering voluntary buyouts to about 60,000 employees, roughly a quarter of its workforce, as it tries to control costs while spending heavily on artificial intelligence infrastructure. The Voluntary Exit Offer was announced Monday in a memo from Amy Coleman, Microsoft's executive vice president and chief people officer, and posted on Microsoft's official blog.

The offer is open to employees at level 70 and below in participating teams in the United States, Canada, India and the United Kingdom, the company told GeekWire. Microsoft counted 223,000 full-time employees as of June 30, down from 228,000 a year earlier, before its July layoffs.

"This offer gives eligible employees who may be considering a future outside the company a new choice to make that transition now with support."

— Amy Coleman, Microsoft Chief People Officer

Who Is Eligible, and What the Package Includes

Level 70 includes general managers and some employees with vice president titles, but not corporate vice presidents, GeekWire reported. There is no age or tenure requirement this time, and performance is not a factor. A source familiar with the matter told Reuters the offer will affect divisions including AI experiences, Copilot, finance, human resources, Xbox and Windows + Devices, and will exclude units such as marketing, commercial business and security. Microsoft's sales organization is not participating, nor are some engineering groups and corporate functions, according to GeekWire.

https://youtube.com/watch?v=ZZOIDKPyI3A

The package is equivalent to Microsoft's standard severance, the company said, including base pay based on tenure and level, continued stock vesting, healthcare coverage for a fixed period and career transition services. It does not include the extended healthcare that was a major draw of the earlier retirement program. Eligible employees were told they would receive an email with their offer details within hours, and they have until the first week of December to decide, GeekWire reported.

A Broader Follow-Up to the Spring Retirement Offer

The new program builds on Microsoft's first-ever Voluntary Retirement Program this spring, which was limited to U.S. employees at senior director level 67 and below whose age plus years at the company met a minimum threshold. About 30% of the roughly 8,750 eligible U.S. employees took that deal, and Microsoft disclosed a $900 million charge for the retirement program in its April earnings report, according to GeekWire. Microsoft told GeekWire it expects a much smaller share to accept this time, because the broader offer is not aimed at longtime employees close to retirement.

Microsoft said the offer is not a sign that it needs fewer employees overall, and a spokesperson described it as one of several ways the company is adjusting to changing business needs. The company also said the offer is not a replacement for layoffs, which will remain part of its approach depending on conditions. Microsoft cut 4,800 jobs in July, about 2% of its global workforce, followed by hundreds more in September, after cutting more than 15,000 jobs in 2025.

Why Microsoft Is Doing This Now

Like its peers, Microsoft is under pressure from Wall Street to hold down operating expenses as it pours tens of billions of dollars into data centers and AI infrastructure, GeekWire reported. Offering voluntary exits lets participating organizations adapt their workforce without selecting individuals for involuntary cuts in those groups, while employees who were already considering leaving get financial support and career planning resources to do so now.

For Microsoft's large workforce in India, and for Indian employees in the United States, Canada and the United Kingdom, the offer applies on the same terms as for other staff: eligibility depends on team participation and level, not nationality, and the decision deadline is the first week of December.

What Happens Next

Microsoft reports quarterly earnings on Wednesday afternoon, which could include projections for the cost of the new buyout offer, GeekWire reported. The company has not provided a projection for how many employees will accept. Coleman wrote that Microsoft will keep helping employees build new skills and, where it makes sense, find new opportunities across the company, noting that Microsoft said in July it had redeployed more than 4,000 employees into new roles over the previous year.
